---
title: "Email bodies"
description: "Render HTML and plain-text email from the same templates as your site."
---

An email needs an HTML body and a plain-text one. Render both from templates, with
`PageTemplate` for HTML and `PageTextTemplate` for text. A text template uses the same
`${...}` expressions but doesn't escape HTML or parse tags.

```{python}
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplate, PageTextTemplate

html_body = PageTemplate("""\
<p>Hi ${user},</p>
<p>Your order <strong>#${order.id}</strong> has shipped:</p>
<ul><li tal:repeat="item order.items">${item}</li></ul>
""")

text_body = PageTextTemplate("""\
Hi ${user},

Your order #${order.id} has shipped:
${'\\n'.join('- ' + item for item in order.items)}
""")


class Order:
    id = 1042
    items = ['Rust & Python mug', 'Sticker <3']


print(html_body(user='Ada', order=Order()))
print(text_body(user='Ada', order=Order()))
```

The HTML body escapes `&` and `<`, and the text body leaves them alone.

In an app, keep the email templates in your template folder (for example `emails/`), and
load them with `PageTemplateLoader`, or `PageTextTemplateFile` for the text version.
Emails can use partials too. `render_partial` works in any template, so the footer you share
with the site can live in one file:

```html
<p>Hi ${user},</p>
...
${render_partial('emails/_footer.pt', unsubscribe_url=unsubscribe_url)}
```

Then pass the two strings to your mail library, such as `email.message.EmailMessage`'s
`set_content()` and `add_alternative(..., subtype='html')`.
